source.title: Generalizable Prompt Learning via Gradient Constrained Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Liang-Chen Liu; Nan Wang; Da-Wei Zhou; De-Cheng Liu; Xi Yang; Xin-Bo Gao; Tong-Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures prompt-learning generalization and loss-landscape properties in vision-language models, a distinct setting from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports seen-class and unseen-class accuracy and qualitative loss-landscape comparisons. Its unseen-class results concern class-disjoint transfer, and it does not report the train/test error gap, fitting random labels, or magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flatness–generalization rationale to develop prompt optimization and reports its methods' performance. It does not test any specified version: its landscape visualizations and class-disjoint transfer accuracies do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or training–test error gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors argue that both loss value and loss sharpness matter for maintaining seen-class performance while improving unseen-class performance, and propose GCSCoOp to optimize both through gradient constraints. Their evidence concerns prompt transfer, not the specific generalization measures in V7.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a small set of prompts for a frozen pretrained CLIP model and evaluates seen-to-unseen class and cross-domain transfer; it does not use the claim versions’ natural-label, random-label, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, or memorized-example tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that perturbation radius and gradient-constrain thresholds affect seen/unseen performance; it also reports dataset-specific hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 11 datasets, CoOp achieves 82.68% seen and 64.15% unseen accuracy; SCoOp achieves 79.29% and 72.52%; GCSCoOp achieves 82.46% and 73.95%. These are prompt-method comparisons on disjoint class groups.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-constrained SAM can improve unseen-class accuracy while largely maintaining seen-class accuracy in few-shot frozen-CLIP prompt learning.

fits_no_version.finding: On the selected DTD visualization, SCoOp and GCSCoOp have qualitatively flatter landscapes than CoOp, with losses 1.0225 and 0.2675 versus 0.1089. GCSCoOp combines a flatter landscape with lower loss than vanilla SCoOp.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss value and qualitative landscape flatness jointly inform the seen/unseen accuracy trade-off in prompt learning.

record.problems: The reported main accuracy aggregates do not include uncertainty estimates. The loss-landscape relationship is presented through selected visualizations and qualitative descriptions; no train/test error gap or magnitude-aware sharpness measure is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant reported outcomes were left out. Cross-domain target-dataset results concern out-of-distribution transfer and do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Network widening beyond the width required for zero training error, with convergence and test-error measurements. Increasing prompt token count does not establish these conditions.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks trained from scratch and interventions on local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and their interactions with dataset size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text is arXiv:2309.07866v2 from September 2023; this verdict applies to that text. Seen-class evaluation accuracy is not training accuracy, so subtracting seen and unseen accuracies would not produce V7's generalization gap. No omitted result tests a specified version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance for the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning conditions.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of train/test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
